Each Kirby MCQ item text states its own immediate/delayed amounts and delay, so it implies a discount rate k=(LDR-SIR)/(SIR*delay). Parsed k from our item_text for all 27 items and correlated it with the live proportion choosing the delayed option (resp=2): Spearman rho=+0.961, Pearson on log k =+0.961, in the correct direction, with the extremes exactly as theory requires (k=0.00016 items: 4-7% choose delayed; k=0.25 items: 97%). Items sharing a k differ only by reward magnitude, the expected magnitude effect. A permuted item_text mapping would destroy this relationship, so this is a strong item-by-item verification. Also confirms the codes follow canonical Kirby ordering (mc1 = $54 vs $55/117d).

route: route 6 (keying polarity) + route 8 (semantic coherence of item means), used to adjudicate variable-label vs column-name (issue #1654)
evidence: Name-vs-label conflict resolved in favour of the labels, decisively. (1) Coherence: the 10 labels, read in column order, reproduce the RSES in the standard circulated administration order (canonical Rosenberg-1965 items 7,3,9,4,5,10,1,8,6,2), i.e. a known permutation, not a scramble; the column names follow the Rosenberg-1965 order 1..10. Names and labels agree only on dowell304, noproud305, morerespect308. (2) Keying polarity on the raw, unreversed data (N=374 complete cases): the correlation matrix splits into a positive block {301,302,304,306,307,308} and a negative block {303,305,309,310} (e.g. r(302,304)=+0.39, r(302,307)=+0.39, r(303,309)=+0.26, r(309,310)=+0.30, r(302,310)=-0.19, r(303,304)=-0.28). The two hypotheses differ on exactly four columns, and the data agree with the LABEL hypothesis on all four: 302 positive (label 'number of good qualities'; the name nogood302 would predict negative), 303 negative (label 'I am a failure'; name goodqualities303 would predict positive), 306 positive (label 'positive attitude'; name usefull306 would predict negative), 310 negative (label 'no good at all'; name positiveattitude310 would predict positive). (3) Means corroborate: 303=1.47 and 309=1.55 (near-floor, correct for 'failure'/'useless') while 302=3.28 and 306=3.19 (near-ceiling, correct for 'good qualities'/'positive attitude') -- the reverse of what the column names imply. morerespect308 sits with the positive block (r=+0.20..+0.33) despite negative wording, the well-documented behaviour of that RSES item in this very sample (the paper drops it, alpha .61 -> .72, citing Schmitt & Allik's Ethiopian alpha of .33); both hypotheses assign it the same text, so it is not diagnostic either way. (4) Anchor direction cross-checked against the sibling PSS-10 in the same .sav (0 Never..4 Very Often, unambiguous): under the .sav's RSES value labels (1 Strongly Disagree..4 Strongly Agree, as used by the processing script) the positive-worded RSES block correlates -0.28 with the distress-worded PSS items and +0.39 with the coping-worded ones, and the negative block flips both signs (+0.40 / -0.24) -- the expected pattern. The paper's Methods sentence '1 (strongly agree) to 4 (strongly disagree)' is therefore wrong for the archived data and was not followed.

route: positional header diff (core model 3) + questionnaire item numbering
evidence: data/bakumenko_2023_adyghe_values.py assigns item_1..item_7 positionally from all_cols[7:14] (after id is inserted at position 0). Re-read the source workbook: positions 6..12 of the raw file are exactly the seven 'Оцените важность...' headers, in the order ethics/native language/Nart epics/rituals and dances/national dress/national cuisine/national sports -- identical to the script's ITEM_TEXT dict and to rows 1-7 of Таблица 2 in the study's own questionnaire PDF. Per-item response distributions from the raw .xlsx match the live table cell for cell (item_1 3/4/5 = 2/13/136; item_3 2/3/4/5 = 1/2/17/131; item_7 2/3/4/5 = 8/16/46/81), confirming both the column selection and that no shift occurred.

Neither the .xlsx (headers S1..S10, 'Data dictionary' sheet scale-level only) nor the paper ties any code to an item, so the order was reconstructed and tested. Raw, unreversed responses (N=37) split cleanly by sign into a positive block {S1,S2,S4,S6,S7} and a negative block {S3,S5,S9,S10} (e.g. r(S1,S4)=+0.73, r(S6,S7)=+0.66, r(S3,S5)=+0.54, r(S9,S10)=+0.58, r(S1,S9)=-0.69, r(S5,S6)=-0.64). That polarity pattern is incompatible with the Rosenberg-1965 numbering (which would predict positives at 1,3,4,7,10) and matches exactly the standard administered RSES order used by the Korean version (canonical items 7,3,9,4,5,10,1,8,6,2 -> positives at positions 1,2,4,6,7), which is the order shipped. S8 is the marker: near-zero correlations with the positive block (-0.19..+0.17) but +0.50 with S10, the known misbehaviour of 'I wish I could have more respect for myself', which sits at position 8 in that order -- and the same item behaves the same way in bakker_2020_rses. Item means corroborate (S9 'I certainly feel useless at times' is the lowest at 1.65 with 20/37 at floor; S8 the highest at 2.70). Verifies polarity class and the position of S8, not the order within each polarity class, so adjacent same-polarity swaps (e.g. S1 vs S2) are not independently excluded beyond the published order.

route: route 6 attempted (keying polarity) - UNAVAILABLE; route 7 marker item + alpha match only
evidence: Polarity route dead: all 45 inter-item correlations are positive (+0.12 to +0.63) and every item-total is positive, i.e. the five negatively worded items are stored already reversed, so no sign pattern distinguishes them. An exhaustive search over all 252 possible 5-item subsets found NO reverse-wording method factor either (canonical negative set {2,5,6,8,9}: mean within-group r = 0.263/0.304, mean cross-group r = 0.315 -- no separation). Remaining, weak, corroboration: (a) RSES8 has the lowest mean of the ten (1.53 of 3, next lowest 1.70), matching the well-documented marker behaviour of RSES item 8 ('I wish I could have more respect for myself'); (b) computed Cronbach alpha = 0.805 matches the paper's reported RSES alpha of 0.81 exactly, confirming the block is the RSES; (c) RSES1 has the highest mean (2.24), as expected for item 1. None of this rules out a permuted administration order of the kind found in bakker_2020_rses. ORCHESTRATOR ADDITION 2026-08-18: position 8 now has positive support. RSES8 has both the lowest mean (1.53) and the lowest item-rest correlation (0.36 vs 0.40-0.57 for the rest), which is the known signature of Rosenberg item 8 ('I wish I could have more respect for myself'), the scale's classic misfitting item; the same item showed the same signature at position 8 in bang_2023_self_esteem, and in the permuted bakker_2020_rses file position 8 was one of the three columns whose name and label agreed. Live aggregates confirm the merge: 27,613 distinct items contiguous 1..27613, not 27,613 + 948 = 28,561; items 1-948 median n = 2,515 vs 396 for items 949-27,613 (6.35x, ~1.89M excess rows, against train_task_3_4.csv's 1,382,727 answers over 948 questions). Codes 1-948 each pool two different questions. Resp axis is likewise broken: the script renames AnswerValue (1-4 option choice) to IsCorrect for the task-2 test files, giving resp = {0,1,2,3,4} with all five levels present on 22,468 of 27,613 items. This establishes that the codes are ambiguous; it establishes nothing about any item's text, because none exists. Computed via irw_table_sets() server-side; the 24,076,951-row table was never fetched.

route: item-code derivation re-run against the source file (per-item n, 5730 items) + rival-hypothesis contrast; no text axis to test
evidence: NO ITEM TEXT SHIPPED, so no item_text<->item mapping exists to verify - status is NO_ROUTE on that axis by construction, not for want of a route. What the script does establish is the referent of the bare integer item code: item = 1-based rank of QuestionId ascending. Live per-item n (irw_table_sets server-side aggregate, no export) vs count of non-missing IsCorrect rows per QuestionId in checkins_lessons_checkouts_training.csv: 0 of 5730 items mismatch (item 1 = QuestionId 31769, n 50 vs 50; item 2 = 31770, 44 vs 44; item 5730 = 147933, 6 vs 6). The rival first-appearance-order hypothesis mismatches 5676 of 5730, so the check has teeth. Whole-table totals also agree: 509,957 rows, 5,730 questions, 6,468 users. This does NOT establish any item wording, and the n-vector is degenerate - only 133 of 5730 items have an n no other item shares, so a swap of two same-n items would go undetected; it rules out wholesale re-orderings only.

route: re-run of the processing script over the source data file (core model 3, pattern 4), cross-checked by route 9 response-frequency matching
evidence: data/short_dark_triad.R assigns item = row_number() over unique(item) after pivot_longer, so item k must be the k-th column of the SD3 deposit's data.csv with country/source dropped: M1-M9, N1-N9, P1-P9. route: re-ran the processing script's derivation over the original source file (core model section 3, script-generated integer codes)
evidence: data/vocabulary_iq.R assigns item = row_number() over the pivoted column order, so the claim under test is items 1-45 = VIQT_data.csv columns Q1..Q45 and items 46-75 = columns S1..S30. Re-running that derivation over the public source file (openpsychometrics.org/_rawdata/VIQT_data.zip, 12173 rows) reproduces four per-item fingerprints of the live table exactly, for all 75 items: non-missing n (item 1/Q1 12161 vs 12161; item 27/Q27 6865 vs 6865; item 43/Q43 6220 vs 6220; item 46/S1 12092 vs 12092), number correct (item 1 11956 vs 11956; item 4/Q4 5207 vs 5207; item 43 3271 vs 3271; items 46-75 all 0 vs 0), and - because the live `id` is row_number() over the same raw file - the sum and sum-of-squares of the respondent ids that answered each item (item 1 sum_id 74037299 vs 74037299; item 62/S17 73398319 vs 73398319). 75 of 75 items match on all four, and the 75 fingerprints are mutually distinct, so the match distinguishes every item from every other rather than only reproducing the set. That distinctness is what separates the four supplemental groups (S27/S28 both n=12047, S14/S19 both 12049, S20/S21 both 12051, S7/S8/S17 all 12061) whose resp is uniformly 0 and which n alone leaves tied: their id sums differ (73280877 vs 73303337; 73319155 vs 73301720; 73317990 vs 73341155; 73407532 vs 73389114 vs 73398319). Scope: this settles the item-to-column mapping. The wording itself is a transcription of the dataset's own codebook, and the two section_prompt strings come from the test page's Procedure paragraph and the codebook's one-line description of the supplemental scale rather than from the administered form. Re-runnable as verify_vocabulary_iq.R (VERDICT: PASS).

evidence: Code derivation: item IS the source column name -- data/wang_2024_speaking_self_efficacy.py selects the 13 item columns BY NAME from S1 Data (journal.pone.0297517.s004, sheets Study2-efa 224 + Study2-cfa 295) and melts them, so no positional assignment occurs in IRW. Route 9 (label->code direction): all 91 of the 13 item x 7 resp cell counts in the live table reproduce the deposit's columns exactly (L1 disagreement 0; e.g. VE3 2,10,27,54,150,170,106 deposit vs live), and the 13 response profiles are mutually distinct (closest pair SP2/SP3 at L1=18), so no live<->deposit column permutation is possible. Route 5 (subscale blocks, server-side CORR self-join, n=519): 13/13 items have their weakest within-block r above their strongest cross-block r; within-block mean r +0.750 (min +0.615) vs cross-block mean +0.144 (max +0.594), so the test is powered, not a general-factor artifact. This confirms the S3 Appendix's four headed blocks ME(4)/VE(3)/SP(3)/PES(3) map onto the ME/VE/SP/PES column prefixes. Route 6 (polarity): the 3 negatively worded PES items correlate -0.137/-0.191/-0.216 with the 10 positively worded items while all 10 of those correlate +0.420..+0.571 with each other, so PES is stored RAW and the shipped negative wording matches the data direction. Corroboration: CFA-phase (cov_study='cfa', N=295) per-item mean range 3.722-5.871 and SD range 1.042-1.500 reproduce the paper's stated 3.72-5.87 and 1.04-1.50 exactly. WHAT THIS DOES NOT ESTABLISH: the S3 Appendix numbers items 1..13 CONTINUOUSLY under subscale headings and never prints the code strings ME1/ME2/..., so the numeric suffix is inferred from print order within a block -- this is a block-level label match, not a code-level one, and the standing 'explicit code labels in the paper' exemption does not reach the suffix. Nothing here distinguishes ME1 from ME2 or SP1/SP2/SP3; 4!*3!*3!*3! = 5184 within-block orderings survive every number above. Rival routes tried and failed: the paper's Tables 4/5 give loadings/alpha/CR/AVE per FACTOR only, never per item (route 1 unavailable); cross-instrument content matching on the deposit's Study3 sheet (n=304 who answered both scales) is swamped by a general factor (ME2 vs its content twin LSE5 r=.530 but ME2 vs PSE2 r=.591), so it does not recover within-block order.

route: explicit subscale-code labels in S2 Appendix + code-is-source-column-name derivation + live-vs-deposit per-item aggregate identity + paper Fig 2 per-item CFA loading reproduction (route 1-style); cross-instrument content correlations (route 8) attempted and underpowered
evidence: Code derivation: data/wang_2024_speaking_self_efficacy.py selects the S1 Data columns BY NAME (LSE1..PSE4) and melts with var_name='item' -- the live item code IS the source column header, no rename and no positional assignment (core model s3 row 1). Live-vs-deposit: a server-side GROUP BY aggregate on the live table (redivis query, no export) reproduces every deposit column exactly for all 15/15 items over the pooled 227 efa + 289 cfa = 516 respondents -- mean/sd to <0.005 (LSE1 4.00/1.23, LSE3 3.41/1.17, DSE2 3.53/1.30, PSE4 4.39/1.36), max, and the integer count of resp=7 (LSE1 7, LSE2 9, LSE3 0, LSE4 1, LSE5 6, SRE1 17, SRE2 28, SRE3 31, DSE1 11, DSE2 10, DSE3 24, PSE1 16, PSE2 13, PSE3 10, PSE4 32); LSE3 is the only item never rated 7 (max 6) in both, and the SRE2/SRE3 mean tie at 4.94 is broken by sd 1.23 vs 1.18 and n7 28 vs 31. Authors' own labels: paper Fig 2 prints per-item standardized CFA loadings against these codes (N=289, deposit sheet Study1-cfa); refitting the 4-factor correlated model reproduces all 15 to <=0.005 (LSE1 .842 vs .84, LSE3 .705 vs .70, DSE1 .903 vs .90, PSE2 .908 vs .91, PSE4 .733 vs .73), and 13 of 15 are distinct within their own block (LSE4 and LSE5 both .81). Text side: S2 Appendix prints the 15 items numbered 1-15 CONTINUOUSLY under four subscale headers -- 'Linguistic Self-Efficacy (LSE)' items 1-5, 'Self-Regulatory Efficacy (SRE)' 6-8, 'Delivery Self-efficacy (DSE)' 9-11, 'Performance Self-Efficacy (PSE)' 12-15; block sizes 5/3/3/4 match the deposit's column counts and the paper's Table 1. The string 'LSE' occurs EXACTLY ONCE in the appendix's document.xml, in that header: no per-item code is printed anywhere in the file. So the standing 'explicit code labels in the paper' exemption holds for the SUBSCALE PREFIX only -- the numeric suffix is the item's position inside its labelled block, i.e. a positional inference. Attempted and underpowered: cross-instrument content pairing on the deposit's Study3 sheet (N=304, same respondents took both scales) -- ME2 ('correct pronunciation, intonation, and liaison') should peak on the identically worded LSE5 but the LSE-block max is LSE1 r=0.564 vs LSE5 r=0.530, and ME4 ('excellent grades on Spoken English tests') should peak on PSE4 but the PSE-block max is PSE3 r=0.693 while PSE4 is the block MINIMUM r=0.499; a general factor dominates all 195 cross-scale correlations, so this is a failure of the test rather than evidence against the mapping. NOT ESTABLISHED: the within-block ordering. Nothing here distinguishes LSE1 from LSE2 (or the order within SRE, DSE, PSE); rotating the five LSE texts among LSE1..LSE5 would leave every number above unchanged. What IS established: every item's subscale membership, by the appendix's own block labels, and the identity of the live code with the deposit column the paper itself labels. CAVEAT ON PROVENANCE: the shipped provenance note claims the appendix uses 'the same LSE/SRE/DSE/PSE codes the response columns use, so no positional inference'; that is true of the prefix and false of the suffix. No sign that anything shipped is wrong -- the appendix's print order and the deposit's column order agree block for block -- but the mapping is corroborated, not label-matched, at item level.

route: route 3 (published scale total reproduced) + route 5/6-style structural check (published correlated-error pair) + route 1 cross-sample per-item mean/SD profile; see verify_campos_2023_oes.R
evidence: Block membership is settled outright: the paper's S2 Table publishes the OES score as 7.01 (SD 1.58) for Finland and 7.13 (SD 1.74) for Brazil, and the mean of columns OES01-OES07 in the deposit reproduces 7.010/1.579 and 7.127/1.742 (max deviation 0.003), so the seven columns this table carries are the OES block and not PIDAQ or SWLS. The paper's S1 Table reports that the OES factor model was refined 'adding a correlation between errors of items 1 and 2' in both countries, and Campos et al. 2020 names those as items 1 (face) and 2 (facial profile), the only two non-dental items; in the data the largest 1-factor residual correlation is OES01-OES02 at +0.194, with the next pair (OES04-OES05) at +0.082, so OES01 and OES02 are pinned as the facial pair. Content structure agrees: OES03 (mouth) is the bridge, correlating 0.655 with OES01 against OES04's 0.506, while OES04-OES05 (rows of teeth, tooth shape) is the tightest dental pair at 0.770. Per-item profile against the same authors' independent OES-Pt validation sample (Campos et al. 2020 PeerJ Table 3, n=537, same instrument and language): Spearman 0.91 on means and 0.93 on SDs across the 7 items, with OES06 the lowest mean (6.23 vs published 6.1, color of teeth), OES07 the highest (7.94 vs 7.4, gum) and OES01 the lowest SD (1.88 vs 2.0, face). What this does NOT establish: this study published no per-item table, so the assignment WITHIN the pinned facial pair (OES01 face vs OES02 facial profile) and within the dental block OES03-OES05 rests on a cross-sample descriptive profile, not on an in-sample published statistic -- a swap of OES01/OES02 or of OES03/OES04 would be contradicted by that profile but not by anything in this paper, which is why the status is PARTIAL rather than VERIFIED. It also establishes nothing about the option_text axis beyond the paper's own statement that 0 = very dissatisfied and 10 = very satisfied (resp 1-9 ship blank), and nothing about the Finnish or Portuguese wording, which this table does not ship.
